epithet: Woe, that Day, to the deniers
lede: It came down in a cave at Minā, and it was the last surah Umm al-Faḍl ever heard the Prophet ﷺ recite. One line returns in it ten times, after each proof and each scene, like the tolling of a bell.

names.name: al-Mursalāt
names.note: After the oath it opens with. Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and Qatādah said they are the winds, sent one after another; others, the angels sent with Allah’s command. The Companions called the surah Wa-l-mursalāt, or Wa-l-mursalāti ʿurfan.

revelation.detail: The majority hold all of it to be Makkan. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatādah and Muqātil that one ayah is Madinan: “When it is said to them, ‘Bow’, they do not bow” (77:48). Its place of revelation is known more exactly than that of almost any other surah: Ibn Masʿūd was there.
revelation.when: Makkah: a cave at Minā, with the Prophet ﷺ and a group of his Companions

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ المُرْسَلاتِ مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّها في قَوْلِ الجُمْهُورِ وَحُكِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، وقَتادَةَ، ومُقاتِلٍ أنَّ فِيها آيَةً مَدَنِيَّةً
عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ -هُوَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ-قَالَ: بَيْنَمَا نَحْنُ مَعَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ، فِي غَارٍ بِمِنًى، إِذْ نَزَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ: " وَالْمُرْسَلاتِ " فَإِنَّهُ لَيَتْلُوهَا

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ والنَّحّاسُ، وابْنُ مَرْدُويَهَ والبَيْهَقِيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ المُرْسَلاتِ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by Ibn al-Ḍurays, al-Naḥḥās, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī.

attested.quote: هي مَكِّيَّةٌ في قَوْلِ الحَسَنِ، وعِكْرِمَةَ، وعَطاءٍ، وجابِرٍ
attested.says: Makkan, in the saying of al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrimah, ʿAṭāʾ and Jābir ibn Zayd.

setting: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd tells it. “We were with the Prophet ﷺ in a cave at Minā when ‘Wa-l-mursalāt’ came down upon him. He was reciting it, and I was taking it from his mouth while his mouth was still moist with it, when a snake sprang out at us. The Prophet ﷺ said, ‘Kill it.’ We rushed at it and it got away. He said: ‘It has been spared your harm, as you have been spared its harm.’”
So we know the place, and who was present, and that the surah was learned by its first hearers at the very moment of its arrival.

Its construction is unlike anything else in the Qurʾan. A short passage — the end of the stars and the mountains; the destruction of earlier peoples; the making of man from a lowly fluid; the earth that holds the living and the dead; the shadow of the Fire that gives no shade; the gardens of the mindful — and after each one the same sentence: “Woe, that Day, to the deniers.” Ten times. The effect is of a case being made point by point before a court, with the verdict read out after every piece of evidence.
And it ends with a question that has never been answered: in what message, after this one, will they believe?

occasions.title: The cave at Minā
occasions.text: “While we were with the Prophet ﷺ in a cave at Minā, ‘Wa-l-mursalāt’ was sent down upon him. He was reciting it and I was receiving it from his mouth, his mouth still moist with it, when a snake leapt out at us…”
occasions.source: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: al-Bukhārī (1830, 4930) and Muslim (2234).

aim: To establish the Resurrection by confronting the deniers with proofs — each followed by threat and warning.

outline.title: The oath
outline.summary: By those sent forth one after another, storming on with force; by those that scatter far and wide, then separate one thing from another, then deliver a reminder — to excuse or to warn: what you are promised will surely come to pass.

outline.title: The Day of Decision
outline.summary: When the stars are put out, the sky is torn open, the mountains are blown away and the messengers are given their appointed time — for what Day has it been deferred? For the Day of Decision. Woe, that Day, to the deniers.

outline.title: Three proofs
outline.summary: Did We not destroy the earlier peoples, and then send the later ones after them? Did We not create you from a lowly fluid, lodged in a secure place for a known term? Did We not make the earth a container for the living and the dead, and set on it lofty mountains, and give you sweet water to drink? After each: woe, that Day, to the deniers.

outline.title: “Go to what you used to deny”
outline.summary: Go to a shadow of three columns, which gives no shade and no defence against the flame; it throws out sparks like fortresses, like tawny camels. This is a Day they will not speak, nor be allowed to make excuses. This is the Day of Decision; We have gathered you and those of old. If you have any plot, then plot against Me.

outline.title: The mindful, and the last question
outline.summary: The mindful will be among shades and springs, with whatever fruit they desire. As for you: eat and enjoy yourselves a little — you are guilty. When they are told to bow, they do not bow. In what message, after this, will they believe?

keyAyah.why: The surah’s last word, and its challenge: if not this, then what?

virtues.text: Umm al-Faḍl heard her son Ibn ʿAbbās reciting “Wa-l-mursalāti ʿurfan” and said: “My son, by your recitation of this surah you have reminded me: it is the last thing I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He was reciting it in the sunset prayer.”
“Hūd, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ‘ʿAmma yatasāʾalūn’ and ‘Idhā l-shamsu kuwwirat’ have turned me grey.”

before: Al-Insān described at length what is prepared for the righteous. Al-Mursalāt turns to those who deny that anything is prepared at all.
after: This surah ends: in what message after this will they believe? Al-Nabaʾ opens on the same people, still asking one another about the great news.

notable.label: The Day of Decision; woe to the deniers

sources: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim; Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī
